<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Subgroups of <math id="m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> Induce Natural RNN and Transformer Architectures</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Joshua Nunley
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Cognitive Science Program &amp; Department of Informatics
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Indiana University
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">joshnunl@iu.edu</span></a>
</span></span></span></span></div>
<div class="ltx_dates">February 20, 2026</div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents a direct framework for sequence models with hidden states on closed subgroups of <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>. We use a minimal axiomatic setup and derive recurrent and transformer templates from a shared skeleton in which subgroup choice acts as a drop-in replacement for state space, tangent projection, and update map. We then specialize to <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> and evaluate orthogonal-state RNN and transformer models on Tiny Shakespeare and Penn Treebank under parameter-matched settings. We also report a general linear-mixing extension in tangent space, which applies across subgroup choices and improves finite-budget performance in the current <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> experiments.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Modern sequence models are built from many interacting architectural choices: update parameterization, stabilization layers, memory mechanisms, and readout conventions. This paper takes a narrower starting point. We assume hidden states and token representations are group-valued, specifically in a closed subgroup of <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, and ask what recurrent and transformer architectures follow directly from that assumption.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The motivation for this choice is methodological. A compact matrix group gives bounded state dynamics by construction, a Lie algebra for local updates, and a natural similarity/readout based on matrix inner products. These ingredients are enough to define complete models without introducing many additional components.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This manuscript has three concrete goals. First, we give a minimal framework and model template based on closed subgroups of <math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>. Second, we show how subgroup choice can be used as a drop-in model design axis for both RNN and transformer templates. Third, we report experiments for one subgroup family, <math id="S1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, using the resulting orthogonal-state RNN and transformer instantiations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work and Positioning</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Orthogonal and unitary RNNs.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A long line of work stabilizes recurrent dynamics by constraining the transition operator to be orthogonal or unitary <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arjovsky et al., 2016</a>, <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wisdom et al., 2016</a>, <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Helfrich et al., 2018</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lezcano-Casado and Martínez-Rubio, 2019</a>)</cite>, with recent variants exploring different parameterizations and update rules <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Biegun et al., 2024</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Alkhairy and others, 2025</a>)</cite>. In all of these models, hidden states remain Euclidean vectors; the group structure constrains the operator, not the state itself.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Manifold-valued states and group-aware attention.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The closest prior direction to ours is SPD-based sequence modeling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Seraphim et al., 2024</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and others, 2023</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubreil et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, where hidden states live on a matrix manifold rather than in <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math>. However, those models use symmetric positive-definite matrices (a symmetric space), not compact group elements with Lie-algebraic tangent updates. Separately, group-aware attention constructions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hutchinson et al., 2021</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fuchs et al., 2020</a>)</cite> and orthogonality constraints on attention operators <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang and Martens, 2026</a>)</cite> use group structure for equivariant processing of inputs, not for the hidden-state dynamics themselves.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">This work.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our contribution is twofold. First, we place both hidden states and token representations directly on a closed subgroup of <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, rather than keeping states in <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math> and constraining operators. Second, we give a shared RNN/transformer template in which subgroup choice is a direct drop-in component—changing the state space, tangent projection, and update map without altering the outer model interface. To our knowledge, neither of these choices has appeared in this combined form for both recurrent and transformer models. We evaluate one instantiation (<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>) under parameter-matched settings.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Framework and Axioms</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G\leq\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G\leq\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> be a closed Lie subgroup with Lie algebra <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. We represent each token <math id="S3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> by a subgroup element <math id="S3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{x_{t}}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{x_{t}}\in G</annotation></semantics></math> and maintain state <math id="S3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}\in G</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use the following minimal assumptions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Causality:</span> <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(H_{t},x_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(H_{t},x_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Group closure:</span> if <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}\in G</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t+1}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t+1}\in G</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Local update:</span> each step is generated by a tangent element in <math id="S3.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{g}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">A standard realization is a multiplicative step generated by the exponential map. Concretely, for any measurable map <math id="S3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{\theta}(H_{t},x_{t})\in\mathfrak{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝔤</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{\theta}(H_{t},x_{t})\in\mathfrak{g}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t+1}=H_{t}\,\Exp\!\big(\Phi_{\theta}(H_{t},x_{t})\big)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.370em;" width="1.370em"><mi>exp</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t+1}=H_{t}\,\Exp\!\big(\Phi_{\theta}(H_{t},x_{t})\big)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p4.2" class="ltx_p">remains in <math id="S3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> by subgroup closure under <math id="S3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Exp(\mathfrak{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝔤</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Exp(\mathfrak{g})</annotation></semantics></math> and group multiplication. We treat this as the construction rule rather than a standalone theorem.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">This gives a single model skeleton across subgroup choices: choose <math id="S3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math>, define <math id="S3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, and read out predictions from <math id="S3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For readout, we use prototype matrices <math id="S3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{v}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{v}\in G</annotation></semantics></math> and logits</p>
<table id="S3.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{v}(H_{t})=\tau\,\Re\,\operatorname{tr}(H_{t}^{\ast}P_{v})+b_{v}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℜ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{v}(H_{t})=\tau\,\Re\,\operatorname{tr}(H_{t}^{\ast}P_{v})+b_{v}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p6.2" class="ltx_p">This is the default subgroup-native readout used throughout this paper.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p7.1" class="ltx_p">From a Riemannian viewpoint, this is the natural local-geometry construction: updates are in tangent space (<math id="S3.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{g}</annotation></semantics></math>), then mapped back to the manifold by <math id="S3.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Exp" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>exp</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Exp</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>General RNN and Transformer Templates</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section defines subgroup-agnostic templates. The subgroup enters only through the state space <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math>, tangent space <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, and projection/update operators.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>RNN template</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given a sequence <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{t})_{t=1}^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{t})_{t=1}^{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, initialize <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{0}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{0}\in G</annotation></semantics></math> and update</p>
<table id="S4.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t+1}=H_{t}\,\Exp\big(U_{t}\big),\qquad U_{t}\in\mathfrak{g}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝔤</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t+1}=H_{t}\,\Exp\big(U_{t}\big),\qquad U_{t}\in\mathfrak{g}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We first construct a raw tangent update</p>
<table id="S4.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{U}_{t}=\Phi_{\theta}(H_{t},M_{x_{t}})\in\mathfrak{g}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝔤</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{U}_{t}=\Phi_{\theta}(H_{t},M_{x_{t}})\in\mathfrak{g},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">then optionally apply a tangent-space map</p>
<table id="S4.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{t}=\Gamma_{\theta}(\widehat{U}_{t}),\qquad\Gamma_{\theta}:\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{g}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>𝔤</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>𝔤</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{t}=\Gamma_{\theta}(\widehat{U}_{t}),\qquad\Gamma_{\theta}:\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{g}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Token logits are computed from <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> with the subgroup-native prototype head</p>
<table id="S4.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{v}(H_{t})=\tau\,\Re\,\operatorname{tr}(H_{t}^{\ast}P_{v})+b_{v}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℜ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{v}(H_{t})=\tau\,\Re\,\operatorname{tr}(H_{t}^{\ast}P_{v})+b_{v}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Transformer template</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each position <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, initialize <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}^{(0)}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}^{(0)}\in G</annotation></semantics></math> from token embeddings. At each layer <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, compute causal attention weights from subgroup similarity scores,</p>
<table id="S4.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{ij}^{(\ell)}=\tau\,\Re\,\operatorname{tr}\!\left((H_{i}^{(\ell)})^{\ast}H_{j}^{(\ell)}\right),\qquad j\leq i," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℜ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em">⁡</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.670em;" width="0.670em"><mi>tr</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>j</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{ij}^{(\ell)}=\tau\,\Re\,\operatorname{tr}\!\left((H_{i}^{(\ell)})^{\ast}H_{j}^{(\ell)}\right),\qquad j\leq i,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<table id="S4.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{ij}^{(\ell)}=\mathrm{softmax}_{j}\big(s_{ij}^{(\ell)}+b_{ij}^{(\ell)}\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>softmax</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{ij}^{(\ell)}=\mathrm{softmax}_{j}\big(s_{ij}^{(\ell)}+b_{ij}^{(\ell)}\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">then apply two subgroup-tangent sub-steps. The <em id="S4.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">attention step</em> updates the state toward the attention-weighted aggregate:</p>

<p id="S4.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The <em id="S4.SS2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">grounding step</em> then adjusts toward the current token embedding:</p>

<table id="S4.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

H_{i}^{(\ell+1)}=\widetilde{H}_{i}^{(\ell)}\,\Exp\big(\Delta_{i,\mathrm{ground}}^{(\ell)}\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ground</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ground</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ground</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ground</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{i,\mathrm{ground}}^{(\ell)}=\Gamma_{\theta,\mathrm{ground}}\!\big(\widehat{\Delta}_{i,\mathrm{ground}}^{(\ell)}\big),\qquad H_{i}^{(\ell+1)}=\widetilde{H}_{i}^{(\ell)}\,\Exp\big(\Delta_{i,\mathrm{ground}}^{(\ell)}\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">In this template we do not introduce separate learned query/key/value maps. The score
<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Re\,\operatorname{tr}((H_{i}^{(\ell)})^{\ast}H_{j}^{(\ell)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℜ</mi><mo lspace="0.337em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>j</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Re\,\operatorname{tr}((H_{i}^{(\ell)})^{\ast}H_{j}^{(\ell)})</annotation></semantics></math>
is already a coordinate-invariant subgroup similarity under global basis changes (conjugation), so attention can be computed directly from the group-valued states.
Final logits come from <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}^{(L)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}^{(L)}</annotation></semantics></math> via the same prototype head as in the RNN template.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Optional tangent mixing component</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both templates include the same optional tangent map component</p>
<table id="S4.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma:\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{g}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>𝔤</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>𝔤</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma:\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{g}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">applied between raw tangent construction and the exponential group step. The intrinsic base case is <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma=\mathrm{Id}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>Id</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma=\mathrm{Id}</annotation></semantics></math>. The symmetry-relaxed variant uses a learned linear map in tangent coordinates:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=\mathrm{vec}_{\mathfrak{g}}(A),\qquad a^{\prime}=Wa,\qquad\Gamma(A)=\mathrm{vec}_{\mathfrak{g}}^{-1}(a^{\prime})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mi>𝔤</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>vec</mi><mi>𝔤</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=\mathrm{vec}_{\mathfrak{g}}(A),\qquad a^{\prime}=Wa,\qquad\Gamma(A)=\mathrm{vec}_{\mathfrak{g}}^{-1}(a^{\prime}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">This applies to recurrent updates and to both transformer sub-steps (attention and grounding).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">With USIM readout, <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> has a concrete channel interpretation. At any state <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>, the readout differential</p>
<table id="S4.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{H}(A)=\left.\tfrac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_{\epsilon=0}\ell(H\Exp(\epsilon A))" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{H}(A)=\left.\tfrac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_{\epsilon=0}\ell(H\Exp(\epsilon A))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">induces a splitting of the tangent space into readout-visible and readout-null directions:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{g}=\underbrace{\ker(D_{H})^{\perp}}_{\text{predictive}}\;\oplus\;\underbrace{\ker(D_{H})}_{\text{memory}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔤</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>ker</mi><mo>⁡</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⟂</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>predictive</mtext></munder><mo rspace="0.502em">⊕</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>ker</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>memory</mtext></munder></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{g}=\underbrace{\ker(D_{H})^{\perp}}_{\text{predictive}}\;\oplus\;\underbrace{\ker(D_{H})}_{\text{memory}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">In tangent coordinates, <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> can therefore reweight and route updates across these two channels before exponentiation. The identity map preserves the raw geometry; a learned linear map can reallocate capacity between channels.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These equations define the templates used in the rest of the paper. Subgroup choice changes the internals of <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, not the outer training interface.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Subgroup Instantiations as Drop-In Components</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The framework applies to any closed Lie subgroup of <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>. In this paper we focus on the following families: <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SU}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>SU</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SU}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SO}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SO}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, and torus models <math id="S5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each subgroup yields a concrete drop-in specification of tangent projection and state update. This section stays at component level; the exact <math id="S5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> equations used in runs are written at the start of the experiments section. Full parameterization recipes for all subgroup families (embedding construction, tangent-map choices, and update-map approximations) are collected in <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Component Approximations and Parameterizations ‣ Subgroups of U(𝑑) Induce Natural RNN and Transformer Architectures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Scope of experiments</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The experiments evaluate <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> models only. The <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> equations are obtained by direct substitution:</p>
<table id="S5.Ex20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(Y)=\tfrac{1}{2}(Y-Y^{\top}),\qquad G=\mathrm{O}(d),\qquad\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{so}(d)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>𝔤</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝔤</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔰</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔬</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(Y)=\tfrac{1}{2}(Y-Y^{\top}),\qquad G=\mathrm{O}(d),\qquad\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{so}(d).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Experiments on <math id="S6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> Models</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate character-level language modeling on Tiny Shakespeare (TS) and Penn Treebank (PTB), reporting bits per character (BPC; lower is better). Unless stated otherwise, models are trained with Adam (learning rate <math id="S6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay <math id="S6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>), batch size 32, gradient clipping at 1.0, and early stopping patience of 50 epochs. Results reported here are single-seed.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All OSM results in the main tables use the subgroup-native USIM readout; linear Euclidean readout appears only in ablations.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Evaluated equations and chosen approximations</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For reported <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> runs, we use</p>
<table id="S6.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(Y)=\mathrm{skew}(Y)=\tfrac{1}{2}(Y-Y^{\top}),\qquad H\leftarrow H\,\Exp(A)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>𝔤</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>skew</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(Y)=\mathrm{skew}(Y)=\tfrac{1}{2}(Y-Y^{\top}),\qquad H\leftarrow H\,\Exp(A).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{H}_{i}^{(\ell)}=H_{i}^{(\ell)}\Exp(Z_{i}^{(\ell)}),\qquad H_{i}^{(\ell+1)}=\widetilde{H}_{i}^{(\ell)}\Exp(G_{i}^{(\ell)})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{H}_{i}^{(\ell)}=H_{i}^{(\ell)}\Exp(Z_{i}^{(\ell)}),\qquad H_{i}^{(\ell+1)}=\widetilde{H}_{i}^{(\ell)}\Exp(G_{i}^{(\ell)}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{\mathrm{attn}},\Gamma_{\mathrm{ground}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>attn</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>ground</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{\mathrm{attn}},\Gamma_{\mathrm{ground}}</annotation></semantics></math> are either identity (no mixing) or learned linear maps in skew-coordinate space (linear mixing), as defined in the general templates. OSM-RNN uses the same pattern with its recurrent tangent update.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Parameter-matched comparisons</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tables <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6.2 Parameter-matched comparisons ‣ 6 Experiments on O(𝑑) Models ‣ Subgroups of U(𝑑) Induce Natural RNN and Transformer Architectures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>–<a href="#S6.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 6.2 Parameter-matched comparisons ‣ 6 Experiments on O(𝑑) Models ‣ Subgroups of U(𝑑) Induce Natural RNN and Transformer Architectures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> compare OSM models against standard baselines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vaswani et al., 2017</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Press et al., 2022</a>)</cite> at fixed parameter budgets. Both the transformer and RNN variants use linear tangent mixing.</p>

<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>Linear mixing and robustness summaries</h3>

<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Among tested update variants, linear mixing is the best-performing option in this <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> setting.
In the table below, “BCH-style intrinsic mix” denotes a second-order Lie-bracket correction update used instead of the learned linear tangent map.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>Tiny Shakespeare, 100K OSMFormer mixing ablation (single-seed, USIM readout fixed across rows).</figcaption>
<table id="S6.T7.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S6.T7.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S6.T7.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt">Mixing mode</th>
<th id="S6.T7.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Params</th>

<td id="S6.T7.2.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb"><span id="S6.T7.2.4.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2.464</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The linear-mixing variant has fewer parameters (91K vs 103K) due to different hidden dimensions in the matched configurations, yet still attains the best BPC.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For optimizer robustness, we also include the 500K Tiny Shakespeare sweep across 9 settings. OSMFormer remains trainable across all tested settings and has a narrower best-validation range than the baseline under the same sweep.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18417v1/ts_robustness.svg" id="S6.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/149;" width="429" height="149"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Optimizer robustness summary on Tiny Shakespeare at 500K parameters (2-layer and 4-layer settings).</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Limitations and Scope</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Experiments focus on character-level Tiny Shakespeare and Penn Treebank and are reported as single-seed runs. The framework itself is subgroup-generic, but this manuscript only validates the <math id="S7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> instantiation in depth. Wider empirical coverage across subgroup families (for example <math id="S7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SU}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>SU</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SU}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>) is left to follow-up work.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Discussion and Future Work</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The current results establish that the subgroup-template construction is usable in practice for the <math id="S8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> case. The next stage is to evaluate what this structure contributes beyond held-out accuracy metrics. We highlight three concrete directions.</p>
</div>
<section id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Interpretability.</h4>

<div id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The model family defines updates in tangent space and then maps them back to the group through <math id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Exp" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>exp</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Exp</annotation></semantics></math>, which creates a direct handle on update geometry. A practical next step is to track per-step tangent magnitudes, per-plane update activity, and attention-vs-grounding contributions during training and inference. On the theory side, these diagnostics can be connected to local linearization of readout and to subgroup-specific coordinate choices for comparing runs across seeds. On the empirical side, the goal is to test whether these quantities are stable and predictive of failure modes, not only descriptive after the fact.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stability.</h4>

<div id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Compact-state dynamics suggest strong training stability, but this should be quantified more systematically. We plan multi-seed robustness sweeps, longer training windows, and broader optimizer regimes (including more aggressive learning-rate and depth settings) under fixed parameter budgets. A parallel theoretical direction is to formalize finite-step sensitivity bounds under subgroup updates and to characterize how stability changes under symmetry-relaxed options such as linear mixing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Memory.</h4>

<div id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The subgroup view naturally induces a memory-design axis: abelian and near-abelian subgroups versus fully non-abelian subgroups imply different interaction patterns in tangent updates. A direct experimental program is to compare these families on tasks with controlled long-range dependencies while holding training protocol and budget constant. A complementary theoretical program is to relate subgroup algebraic structure and update parameterization to measurable memory behavior (retention, transfer, and horizon).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These directions are intentionally incremental: they can be executed within the same template and differ mainly by subgroup drop-ins, readout/mixing choices, and evaluation protocol.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S9" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">9 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presented a direct sequence-model framework built from closed subgroups of <math id="S9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{U}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{U}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>. We gave shared RNN and transformer templates, showed how subgroup choice acts as a drop-in component set, and instantiated the framework concretely on <math id="S9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under parameter-matched settings on Tiny Shakespeare and Penn Treebank, the resulting orthogonal-state RNN and transformer models are competitive with standard baselines. A linear tangent-mixing extension, which applies to any subgroup in the framework, provides the strongest finite-budget performance in the current <math id="S9.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{O}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{O}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> experiments.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The main output of this manuscript is a straightforward construction pipeline: choose a subgroup, plug its tangent projection and update map into the shared templates, and train with the same autoregressive objective. Further subgroup comparisons and larger-scale evaluations are natural next steps.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Component Approximations and Parameterizations</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The main text defines the templates and subgroup drop-in components in exact form.
This section specifies implementation choices for all subgroup families.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>On-group embedding and readout parameterization</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each token <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math>, we keep two trainable parameters:</p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>: input-embedding parameter (used to build <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>),</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>: readout-prototype parameter (used to build <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For matrix-group cases, we first project to the Lie algebra and then exponentiate:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{v}=\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(B_{v}),\qquad Q_{v}=\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(C_{v}),\qquad M_{v}=\Exp(A_{v}),\qquad P_{v}=\Exp(Q_{v})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>𝔤</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>𝔤</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{v}=\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(B_{v}),\qquad Q_{v}=\Pi_{\mathfrak{g}}(C_{v}),\qquad M_{v}=\Exp(A_{v}),\qquad P_{v}=\Exp(Q_{v}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">So <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{v},C_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{v},C_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> are unconstrained parameters, while <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{v},P_{v}\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{v},P_{v}\in G</annotation></semantics></math> are the actual on-group objects used by the model.
The same construction is used for input embeddings (<math id="A1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>) and readout prototypes (<math id="A1.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Compact notation.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To keep formulas readable, we define</p>
